title: Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy, Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor and VS Code Tunnels
clean_text: North Korean state-sponsored actor Kimsuky (aka Velvet Chollima) has expanded its operational toolkit, deploying new malware like HTTPSpy and HelloDoor , alongside leveraging VS Code tunnels in recent attacks against South Korean military and corporate targets. Technical Breakdown: * Threat Actor: Kimsuky (Velvet Chollima), a North Korean state-sponsored advanced persistent threat (APT) group. * Targets: South Korean military and corporate entities. * Attack Period: March and April 2026. * Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs): * Initial Access (Social Engineering): Employed tailored social engineering tactics, specifically spoofing security software installation pages and crafting fake Webex meeting pages. * Malware Deployment: Introduced new malware families: * HTTPSpy: A newly identified tool, likely for reconnaissance, data exfiltration, or further compromise. * HelloDoor: Another new malware, potentially serving as a backdoor or loader for subsequent stages. * Command and Control (C2): Utilized legitimate VS Code tunnels for covert communication, likely for C2 or data exfiltration, leveraging trusted infrastructure to evade detection. Defense: Enhance user awareness training against sophisticated social engineering lures, implement robust network monitoring for unusual outbound connections (e.g., those associated with VS Code tunnels), and ensure EDR/AV solutions are updated to detect new malware families like HTTPSpy and HelloDoor. Source: https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html
